key_insight: Experiments reveal a center-mode elastic instability at vanishing inertia in confined viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow, showing that curved base-flow streamlines are not required.
engineering_relevance: This instability could enable enhanced mixing in low-inertia microfluidic, porous-media, and polymer-processing flows.
method: Drive confined quasi-two-dimensional viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow electromagnetically.
Observe velocity-field structures as forcing strength increases.
Use Oldroyd-B simulations to connect confined-flow dynamics to unbounded-flow center modes.
evidence_signal: Experiments show arrow-shaped velocity structures and increasingly chaotic fluctuations, reproduced in Oldroyd-B simulations and linked to travelling center-mode arrowheads.
watch_item: Generality beyond the confined quasi-two-dimensional setup and the Oldroyd-B model remains to be established.
paper_title: Experimental Evidence of Elastic Instability in Viscoelastic Kolmogorov Flow
